results.title: The free metabelian group $M_n$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the free metabelian group of rank $n$ is the quotient $F_n / F_n''$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators by its second derived subgroup $F_n'' = [F_n', F_n']$, where $F_n' = [F_n, F_n]$ is the derived subgroup of $F_n$.

results.title: Groups whose endomorphisms with non-cyclic images are determined by two elements
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $F$ has this property when there exist elements $g, h \in F$ such that any two endomorphisms $\varphi, \psi$ of $F$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which satisfy $\varphi(g) = \psi(g)$ and $\varphi(h) = \psi(h)$ are equal.

results.title: Shpil'rain's two-element problem for free groups (Kourovka 13.66(a))
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ contains two elements $g$ and $h$ such that any two endomorphisms of $F_n$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which agree at $g$ and at $h$ are equal; that is, $F_n$ has its endomorphisms with non-cyclic images determined by two elements.

results.title: Shpil'rain's two-element problem for free metabelian groups (Kourovka 13.66(b))
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the free metabelian group $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ of rank $n$ (the quotient of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ by its second derived subgroup) contains two elements $g$ and $h$ such that any two endomorphisms of $M_n$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which agree at $g$ and at $h$ are equal.

results.title: Endomorphisms of free groups with non-cyclic images are determined by two elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ contains two elements $g$ and $h$ such that any two endomorphisms $\varphi, \psi$ of $F_n$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which satisfy $\varphi(g) = \psi(g)$ and $\varphi(h) = \psi(h)$ are equal.

results.title: Endomorphisms of free metabelian groups are not always determined by two elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ be the free metabelian group of rank $n$, the quotient of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ by its second derived subgroup. There is an $n$ such that for all elements $g, h \in M_n$ there are endomorphisms $\varphi \ne \psi$ of $M_n$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which satisfy $\varphi(g) = \psi(g)$ and $\varphi(h) = \psi(h)$.

results.title: Covering system
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A covering system of a commutative semiring $R$ is a finite family of cosets $r_i + I_i = \{r_i + a : a \in I_i\}$, where each $I_i$ is an ideal of $R$ different from both $\{0\}$ and $R$, whose union is all of $R$. In the case $R = \mathbb{Z}$, this corresponds to a choice of finitely many congruences $x \equiv r_i \pmod{n_i}$ with moduli $n_i \ge 2$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of them.

results.title: Strict covering system
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A covering system of a commutative semiring $R$, given by cosets $r_i + I_i$, is strict if the ideals $I_i$ are pairwise distinct. In the case $R = \mathbb{Z}$, this means that the congruences defining it have pairwise distinct moduli.

results.title: Asymptotic additive basis of order $n$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $A \subseteq M$ and $n$ a natural number. $A$ is an asymptotic additive basis of order $n$ if all but finitely many elements of $M$ are sums of exactly $n$ (not necessarily distinct) elements of $A$, that is, $M \setminus nA$ is finite, where $nA = \{a_1 + \dots + a_n : a_1, \dots, a_n \in A\}$ and $0A = \{0\}$.

results.title: Exact additive basis of order $n$
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Asymptotic additive basis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $A$ of an additive commutative monoid $M$ is an asymptotic additive basis if there is a natural number $n$ such that $A$ is an asymptotic additive basis of order $n$, that is, all but finitely many elements of $M$ are sums of exactly $n$ (not necessarily distinct) elements of $A$.

results.title: Weak additive basis of order $n$
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Weak additive basis

results.title: Recursion for the Euclidean chain function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $x$ and $y$ with $y \ne 0$, the Euclidean chain function $F$ satisfies $F(x, y) = 1 + F(y, (-x) \bmod y)$, where $(-x) \bmod y$ is the least nonnegative residue of $-x$ modulo $y$.

results.title: Monotonicity criteria for arithmetical structures on coconut trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(d, r)$ be an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ with path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$, and write $d_k = d(v_k)$ and $r_k = r(v_k)$. The following are equivalent: (1) $d_k \ge 2$ for $1 \le k \le p - 1$; (2) $0 < r_2 - r_1 \le r_3 - r_2 \le \cdots \le r_p - r_{p-1}$; (3) $r_1 < r_2 < \cdots < r_p$.

results.title: Characterization of smooth coconut structures
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \ge 1$ and let $(d, r)$ be an arithmetical structure on the coconut tree $CT(p, s)$ with path vertices $v_1, \dots, v_p$ and leaves $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_s$ adjacent to $v_p$. Then $(d, r)$ is smooth if and only if $r(\ell_j) < r(v_p)$ for every $j$ and $r(v_1) < r(v_2) < \dots < r(v_p)$.

results.title: Binary CSP instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A binary CSP instance is a pair consisting of a list $(D_0, \dots, D_{n-1})$ of lists of natural numbers, where $D_j$ is the domain of variable $j$, and a list of constraints, each a triple $(j, k, P)$ of two variable indices $j, k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $P$ of allowed value pairs in $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Well-formed binary CSP instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A binary CSP instance with domain list $(D_0, \dots, D_{n-1})$ and constraint list $C$ is well formed when every constraint $(j, k, P) \in C$ has $j < n$ and $k < n$.

results.title: Feasible binary CSP instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A binary CSP instance with domain list $(D_0, \dots, D_{n-1})$ and constraint list $C$ is feasible when there is a list $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of natural numbers with $a_j \in D_j$ for every $j < n$ and $(a_j, a_k) \in P$ for every constraint $(j, k, P) \in C$, where $a_i$ is read as $0$ for every index $i \ge n$.

results.title: Binary constraint satisfaction as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem BINARY CONSTRAINT SATISFACTION accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of binary CSP instances, to an instance that is well formed and feasible; it rejects every other bitstring, including every bitstring that does not decode.

results.title: BINARY CONSTRAINT SATISFACTION is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem BINARY CONSTRAINT SATISFACTION over bitstrings belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
